newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Santista rationalizes wheat milling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Santista rationalizes wheat milling.

text.p: Brazilian food processor Santista Alimentos has transferred the activities of its wheat mill in Sao Paulo to a larger mill in Santos in order to make economies of scale, a spokeswoman said.
"We are transferring production to the Santos mill," she said. "We are trying to increase our economies of scale."
Santista's Santos mill has a processing capacity of 30,000 tonnes of wheat per month, compared to 3,500 tonnes at the mill in Santo Andre on the outskirts of Sao Paulo.

Santista will continue to manage stocks at the smaller mill, although it could not say how much wheat was being stored there. The future of the mill has not been decided, although Santista plans to retain its stake in it, the spokeswoman said.
Santista, a division of Bunge y Born, has 11 mills in Brazil including the one currently being deactivated. The spokeswoman declined to release an estimate of the firm's total crushing capacity.
